## CELL FACTS

Cell 木_正官 (Wood carrying The Magistrate). Persona The Magistrate (正官). Definition line: "Framework-mediated pressure, the standard that steadies". Keyword Order, charge gentle, poles catalyst Integrity / friction Rigidity. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: the standard that steadies; the frame that holds you holds you in. Arena: the gate, the seal, order, the appointed hour. Classical portrait: framework-mediated pressure; the standard that steadies; rank held by rules, rigidity as the shadow. Ruled domains: Career, Status, Order. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 七杀.
Element arena: Wood (trunk, branch, root, grain, growth, the forest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Earth. structural_interaction seed: "Wood setting standard for Earth cross-polarity — movement asking whether stability is living".
- k2_overview: "Your Wood moves as the Magistrate: living order that grows. You build careers and codes like trellises, principled frames that help everything on them climb. Authority suits you when it nurtures. People accept your rules because your rules have leaves. Prune the dead ones each season and the frame stays believed in."
- k2_functional: "Order is your native climate: you grow straight inside good structure and warp without it."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Stiff","Overformal","Change-proof"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Career":"Your career grows like a managed forest: steady rings, widening responsibility, roots deepening in one good house. Choose organizations you would plant a decade in. Transplanting yearly wastes your kind of compounding.","Status":"Your standing grows organically: respect accruing ring by ring until you are somehow the oak everyone consults. Let it. Just keep lower branches reachable.","Order":"Your order is cultivated: rules as trellises rather than cages, standards that make growing easier. Systems you design get adopted willingly. Revisit them each season so the living thing never outgrows the frame."}

- Sibling cell 木_七杀 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Discipline shaped you the way wind shapes a coastal tree, early and permanently. The training you put yourself through would read as punishment in someone else’s diary. In yours it reads as Tuesday, and the strength it built shows in everything you hold up."

Core element Earth, energy element Wood. Law: Wood tames Earth (木克土: roots hold the hillside). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Wood is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Earth core that shows Wood on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Wood as the Order is the Overfueled band's case (the core has more than it channels); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 土_木's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You keep your word long after it stops being convenient. Being counted on is the respect you want, so you put a promise ahead of your comfort. Add your comfort to the promises you keep, because a word kept at any price wears you down.

value_b.text: Your word is the one thing about you that never moves. Because a kept promise proves you are who you say, you keep your word rather than keep your options open. Say no sooner, and every yes you give keeps its worth.

value.text: Keeping your word matters more to you than keeping your options. Since breaking a promise feels like losing rank with yourself, you stay inside old plans rather than reopen them. Ask out of one dead promise, and you are free when the next chance comes.

value.text: Whoever gives you their word, you expect them to keep it. Because you treat a promise as a rule, you count a missed one as a broken rule instead of a bad week. Allow people one free miss, and your word weighs more for it.

value.text: You earn every step before you take it. Since a handed rank feels borrowed to you, you earn it twice over rather than ask once. When you ask for the next step a little sooner, you stop working a rank below your worth.

value_b.text: A step up counts only once you have earned it. Because an unearned title feels like a coat too big for you, you would rather earn it slowly than be handed it fast. Let one step come to you unearned and keep it anyway.

value.text: You hold the line where letting it slide would be easier. Since you need to know how things stand, you hold the rule ahead of the exception. Let someone else hold one line for a while, instead of carrying every rule alone.

value_b.text: Once you draw a line, you hold it. Since a rule with exceptions is no rule to you, you would sooner let a friend down than drop it. Tell a friend why you hold it, before the line ends up between you.

value.text: Holding the line costs you more than you admit. Since bending a rule feels like losing yourself, you hold it against the people you love as much as against strangers. Bend it once for someone who matters, and you keep a closeness no rule replaces.
